title: Offering Memorandum extraction record
description: The output contract. One object per source document, with a nested tenants[] array at the lease grain. Values here are TYPED (numbers are numbers, dates are ISO); the extraction passes upstream deliberately keep source formatting so a value can be compared to the printed page, and conversion happens once at the emit boundary.

document_id.description: Primary key. OM-YYYY-MM-DD when the source carries a day, OM-YYYY-MM when it only carries a month. Never padded to a fake day.

document_date.description: ISO date or year-month. Never an Excel serial.

document_version.description: Revision state. Precedence Final > Revised > Updated > Draft > Preliminary. Null is the common case. Most OMs carry no revision marker at all. 'Confidential' is a handling classification, not a version, and never appears here.

year_built.description: Kept as a string: sources print ranges and multiple renovation years ('1986/2007/2015-2016'), and collapsing that to one integer discards information.

total_rentable_sf.description: Building RSF as stated in the document. NOT computed from tenants[]. The two legitimately differ (vacancy, non-tenant space, BOMA adjustments), and reconciling them is an analyst's job, not a parser's.

parcel_id.description: Assessor's / tax parcel number as printed. Null when the document prints none, AND when it prints more than one. A property spanning multiple parcels is real, so the record fails closed rather than picking one.

tenant_count.description: Hard rule: MUST equal len(tenants[]). Enforced in code as well as here, because a schema cannot compare two fields.

tenants.description: Lease grain: one row per tenant-in-a-document. A tenant occupying several suites at different terms is several rows. Never collapsed.

contact_names.description: Semicolon-joined listing contacts found in the body. Evidence that the document carries a real listing block; not a contact database.

extraction_confidence.description: Confidence in the DOCUMENT EVIDENCE. High = a parcel ID or a listing contact block was found in the body; Medium = a filename version signal only; Low = inferred.

row_confidence.description: Confidence in HOW THE ROWS WERE READ: High = regex, Medium = LLM over a text layer, Low = OCR then LLM. A different axis from extraction_confidence. A scanned document with a clean printed parcel ID is High on evidence and Low on reading. Kept separate on purpose; collapsing the two loses information a reviewer needs.

notes.description: Audit trail. Issues raised, fallbacks used, and anything a reviewer needs to see.

money.description: Plain number: no currency symbol, no thousands separators, null if absent. A blank cell in the source is null, which is a real state and not an error.

document_id.description: Foreign key. Hard rule: every child document_id MUST equal its parent's. Set from the parent rather than trusted from the row, so the two cannot disagree.

tenant_name.description: As printed, including commas and entity suffixes. Never a subtotal, summary, or space-category label; those are rejected upstream.

pct_of_building.description: Percent as a number: '11.1%' becomes 11.1, not 0.111.

lease_expiration.description: ISO. YYYY-MM when the source prints only a month ('Dec-26'). The day is not in the document and is not invented. YYYY-MM-DD only when the source actually carries a day.

lease_expiration_precision.description: Which precision the source supported. 'month_to_month' records an MTM lease, which has no expiration rather than an unknown one. A distinction that matters to anyone modeling rollover.
